title: 花园门 Huayuan Men
subtitle: Hua Yuan Men, Flower Garden Gate · Xiyang Lou

model.line: Simple massing of a European palace: position and footprint from the ruin, the plan or a survey, heights read from the plates of the 1780s (research/xiyanglou/boxes.csv). Not a detailed model yet; the figures and their methods are in the Dimensions block.
rows: platform 0.3 m, eave 6.7 m, ridge 9 m above the ground
by the stone kit: base, pilasters, arched openings, entablature, balustrade and a glazed roof, as the plates of the 1780s show such fronts; the kit's reading, C, not a detailed model

evidence.title: Plate IV: 花园门 Huayuan Men
evidence.excerpt_other: Aux pieds des colonnes sont deux cippes sur lesquels posent deux lions accroupis,
evidence.summary: Arch with two columns and entablature, two crouching lions on cippi. Panelled wall carried on a small bridge, river below with two more small bridges.

evidence.title: Engraving 4: 花园门 Huayuan Men
evidence.excerpt_other: The wall was of gray brick cut smooth and decorated with a large pattern in pink and a deep cream tint.
evidence.summary: North side of the maze gate, seen from inside; 蓄水楼 visible over the wall. Wall colours as quoted, source of the colours not stated.

evidence.title: 万花阵 and 花园门; 线法山 and 螺蛳牌楼, yaffin 系列02, 13
evidence.summary: Lead: the maze gate 花园门 is shaped like a Western clock case with two brass doors; the maze 89 x 59 m, walls about 1.2 m high and over 1,600 m long; the hill 线法山 has a gate each side, the east one called 螺蛳牌楼. Check against the engravings.

evidence.title: Slips in holder transcriptions of printed titles
evidence.locator: TEI line for Plate_19; V&A O398694
evidence.summary: The plates print 蓄水樓, read in four holders: V&A types 畜水樓 and glosses Chushuilou. Plate 19: Rylands TEI types 線法山門正面十九 with the pinyin Dongmen; V&A types 線法山東門十九, which is what the plate title is by every other holder. NYPL names Castiglione as artist, nobody else does. None changes a tie.

evidence.title: Teng Gu's preface on the photographs and plan
evidence.locator: pp.3-5 of the preface, djvu pages 5-7
evidence.summary: Teng Gu says the photographs and the plan belonged to Ernst Boerschmann and were taken and drawn by Ohlmer, a customs official in Tianjin who lived in Beijing 1867-1879 and whose collection went to the Hildesheim museum. He argues they are earlier than those in Favier's Péking (1897), Combaz 1909, Perzynski 1920 and Münsterberg 1912, naming pages he compared. Fig. 13 is a recent photograph by Zhou Zuanwu; fig. 15 is copied from Favier p.264.

photos.why: Teng Gu: the plan is by Ohlmer too; form agrees with the strip: maze in its court, 谐奇趣 and curved wings, 海晏堂, 方河 and stepped screens.
photos.attribution: Plan by Ernst Ohlmer, from 滕固 Teng Gu 1933, via Wikimedia Commons (CADAL, Sichuan University)
photos.licence: Commons file tag PD-old, shown as "Public domain", on the whole book scan (滕固, 1933; CADAL 11102995, Sichuan University)
photos.visible: whole strip from 谐奇趣 and 黄花阵 in the west to 方河 and 线法墙 in the east; thin dashed lines fan from points, which may be sight lines (not verified)
